content.text: I'll start by reviewing the workspace and pre-gathered resources.

commands.name: axiom-lean-prover
commands.description: Formally verify Lean 4 proofs against Mathlib using the hosted Axiom AXLE API — no local Lean toolchain. Use in the mathematics_lean domain, when a proof needs machine-checked verification but installing Lean/Mathlib locally is undesirable, or when translating informal proofs into formally verified Lean 4 code checked in the cloud. (project)

commands.name: citation-manager
commands.description: Manage BibTeX citations including DOI-to-BibTeX conversion, metadata extraction, validation, and deduplication. Use when building reference lists, converting DOIs to citations, or validating existing .bib files. (project)

commands.name: critical-analysis
commands.description: Evaluate research quality using frameworks like GRADE, bias detection, and logical analysis. Use when assessing paper quality, evaluating claims, or reviewing evidence strength. (project)

commands.name: data-analysis
commands.description: Conduct exploratory data analysis and statistical testing with test selection guidance. Use when exploring datasets, selecting statistical tests, performing power analysis, or preparing results for publication. (project)

commands.name: grant-writing
commands.description: Write research grant proposals with guidance for NSF, NIH, DARPA, and other agencies. Use when preparing grant applications, developing research plans, or writing broader impacts statements. (project)

commands.name: hypothesis-generation
commands.description: Formulate research hypotheses using structured frameworks. Use when developing research questions, designing experiments, or planning studies with testable predictions. (project)

commands.name: literature-review
commands.description: Conduct systematic literature reviews using a structured workflow. Use when starting a new research project, surveying a field, or documenting related work for a paper. (project)

commands.name: paper-finder
commands.description: Find and search for academic papers using the paper-finder service. Use when conducting literature review, searching for related work, finding baseline papers, or looking for methodology references. (project)

commands.name: paper-writer
commands.description: Write academic papers from experiment results using LaTeX. Use when experiments are complete and REPORT.md exists, when asked to write a paper, or when generating publication-ready documents in NeurIPS style. (project)

commands.name: peer-review
commands.description: Conduct structured manuscript reviews with section-by-section checklists and constructive feedback. Use when reviewing papers before submission, providing feedback to colleagues, or preparing reviewer responses. (project)

commands.name: research-brainstorming
commands.description: Creative ideation for research using structured methods like SCAMPER, morphological analysis, and cross-domain analogies. Use when generating research ideas, exploring new directions, or overcoming creative blocks. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a live pane, band, status line, toast or hook inside Claude Code (terminal or desktop Code tab), written as a plugin of function hooks that hot-reloads in this session. Load before writing or debugging a hooks module.

commands.name: team-onboarding
commands.description: Help teammates ramp on Claude Code with a guide from your usage

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

content.text: Now a throughput benchmark for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on CPU with batched greedy decoding.

input.command:
source .venv/bin/activate && python - << 'EOF' 2>&1 | grep -v Warning
import torch, time
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
torch.set_num_threads(32)
m="Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct"
tok=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(m); tok.padding_side="left"
model=AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(m, dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval()
for dt in [torch.bfloat16, torch.float32]:
    model=model.to(dt)

#!/bin/bash
# Prefill-heavy benchmark: bench_prefill.sh <model.gguf> <threads> <parallel>
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
source .venv/bin/activate
LS=tools/llamacpp/llama-b11624/llama-server
$LS -m "$1" --port 18392 -t $2 -tb $2 -np $3 -c $((1024*$3)) -b 2048 -ub 512 --no-webui > logs/llama_benchpf_t$2.log 2>&1 &
SP=$!
for i in $(seq 90); do curl -s localhost:18392/health | grep -q ok && break; sleep 2; done
timeout 400 python - "$3" "$2" << 'PY'
import time, sys, json, concurrent.futures as cf
from openai import OpenAI
c=OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:18392/v1",api_key="x")
n=int(sys.argv[1])
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open("datasets/ag_news_test.jsonl")][:48]
inst="You are a news topic classifier. Read the news article below and decide which topic it belongs to. The possible topics are: World, Sports, Business, Sci/Tech. Respond with only the topic name and nothing else."
def f(r):
    x=c.chat.completions.create(model="x",messages=[{"role":"user","content":inst+"\n\nArticle: "+r["text"]*3+"\n\nTopic:"}],max_tokens=4,temperature=0)
    return x.usage.prompt_tokens, x.usage.completion_tokens
t=time.time()
with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(n) as ex: res=list(ex.map(f,rows))
d=time.time()-t; p=sum(r[0] for r in res)
print(f"threads={sys.argv[2]} par={n} {d:.1f}s prompt_toks={p} -> {p/d:.0f} prompt tok/s, {len(rows)/d:.2f} req/s", flush=True)
PY
kill $SP

Base directory for this skill: /data/summereunann/neurico-workspaces/the_prompt_fragility_index__me_20261014_161052_ad3855b6/.claude/skills/paper-finder

# Paper Finder

Systematic paper discovery and prioritization for research projects.

## When to Use

- Starting a literature review
- Looking for related work on a topic
- Finding baseline papers for experiments
- Searching for methodology references
- Building a citation list for a research paper

## How to Use

Run the helper script from your workspace:

```bash
python .claude/skills/paper-finder/scripts/find_papers.py "your research topic"
```

Options:
- `--mode fast` (default): Quick search
- `--mode diligent`: Thorough search (recommended for comprehensive review)
- `--format json`: Output as JSON instead of text

Example:
```bash
python .claude/skills/paper-finder/scripts/find_papers.py "hypothesis generation with large language models" --mode fast
```

## Search Strategy

### Query Formulation

Use structured queries for better results:

1. **Core concept + Method**: "transformer attention mechanism"
2. **Problem + Domain**: "few-shot learning natural language processing"
3. **Technique + Application**: "graph neural networks drug discovery"

### Multi-Stage Search

1. **Broad scan**: Start with general topic terms
2. **Focused dive**: Use specific method/technique names from initial results
3. **Citation chase**: Search for highly-cited papers referenced in relevant work

## Citation Prioritization

### Relevance Tiers

| Relevance Score | Priority | Action |
|-----------------|----------|--------|
| 3 (High) | Must read | Download PDF, read fully, cite |
| 2 (Medium) | Should read | Read abstract + intro, cite if relevant |
| 1 (Low) | Optional | Skim abstract, cite only if needed |
| 0 (Not relevant) | Skip | Do not include |

### Citation Count Thresholds

| Category | Citation Count | Interpretation |
|----------|----------------|----------------|
| Seminal | 1000+ | Foundational work, must cite |
| Well-established | 100-999 | Widely accepted, cite if relevant |
| Recent/Emerging | 10-99 | Current research, cite for novelty |
| New | <10 | Very recent, check publication venue |

### Venue Tiers (ML/AI Focus)

**Tier 1** (Top venues, high credibility):
- NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, CVPR, ICCV

**Tier 2** (Strong venues):
- AAAI, IJCAI, NAACL, COLING, ECCV, WACV

**Tier 3** (Good venues):
- *ACL workshops, COLM, EACL, CoNLL

**Preprints** (arXiv):
- Check for peer-reviewed version first
- Cite arXiv only if no published version exists

## Screening Workflow

### Phase 1: Title Screening
- Review titles from search results
- Mark papers as "include", "exclude", or "maybe"
- Goal: ~50% reduction

### Phase 2: Abstract Screening
- Read abstracts for included/maybe papers
- Evaluate: relevance, methodology, findings
- Goal: Identify key papers for deeper reading

### Phase 3: Full-Text Review
- Download and read full PDFs for key papers
- Extract: methods, results, limitations, citations
- Use the PDF chunker for detailed reading (see below)

## Output Structure

Returns relevance-ranked papers with:
- Title, authors, year
- Abstract (already extracted)
- URL for download
- Relevance score (0-3, focus on papers with score >= 2)
- Citation count

## After Finding Papers

1. Download PDFs for papers with relevance >= 2
2. Read abstracts first (already provided in output)
3. Only read full PDFs for most relevant papers
4. Write notes to literature_review.md immediately
5. Track citations for references.bib

## Reading Large PDFs

Use the PDF chunker to split papers into smaller PDF files that can be read directly.
This preserves all formatting perfectly (unlike text extraction which loses formatting).

**Dependencies:**
```bash
# Using uv (recommended):
uv add pypdf

# Or with pip:
pip install pypdf
```

**How to run:**

```bash
python .claude/skills/paper-finder/scripts/pdf_chunker.py <pdf_path>
```

Options:
- `--pages-per-chunk N`: Number of pages per chunk (default: 1)
- `--output-dir DIR`: Output directory (default: `<pdf_dir>/pages`)

**Output:**
- Creates PDF chunk files: `<pdf_name>_chunk_001.pdf`, `<pdf_name>_chunk_002.pdf`, etc.
- Creates a manifest: `<pdf_name>_manifest.txt` listing all chunks with page ranges

**Integration with screening workflow:**
1. Run the chunker on papers before detailed reading
2. For abstract skimming: read only chunk 1 (page 1 or pages 1-3)
3. For deep reading: read ALL chunk PDFs sequentially, writing notes after each
4. Check the manifest to see how many chunks exist
5. IMPORTANT: Do not skip chunks - methodology and results are in later chunks

## If Paper-Finder Service Not Running

The script will show a fallback message. Use manual search instead:
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org
- Semantic Scholar: https://www.semanticscholar.org
- Papers with Code: https://paperswithcode.com
- Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com

Manual search works well - paper-finder is just a convenience for faster, more targeted results.

## References

See `references/` folder for:
- `search_strategies.md`: Detailed search query formulation
- `prioritization_guide.md`: Extended prioritization criteria

"""Run the prompt-fragility experiment against a local llama.cpp server (OpenAI-compatible API).

Every (condition, item) response is appended to results/raw/<model_tag>/<task>.jsonl, so the
run is resumable; already-completed (condition, item) pairs are skipped.

Usage:
  python src/run_experiment.py --model-tag qwen2.5-1.5b --port 18393 --n 100 --phase core
"""
import argparse
import concurrent.futures as cf
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from openai import OpenAI

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from perturb import EDIT_TYPES, build_instruction  # noqa: E402
from tasks import TASKS, load_items, score  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

COMBOS = {
    "cosmetic2": ("whitespace", "capitalization"),
    "semantic2": ("synonym", "reorder"),
    "cosmetic3": ("whitespace", "capitalization", "punctuation"),
    "semantic3": ("synonym", "reorder", "typo"),
    "mixed3": ("capitalization", "synonym", "reorder"),
    "all6": tuple(EDIT_TYPES),
}


def conditions(phase, seeds):
    """Return list of (cond_name, edits, seed) for the requested phase."""
    if phase == "core":
        conds = [("original", (), 0)]
        conds += [(f"{e}@{s}", (e,), s) for s in seeds for e in EDIT_TYPES]
        return conds
    if phase == "combos":
        return [(f"{c}@{s}", COMBOS[c], s) for s in seeds for c in COMBOS]
    if phase == "rerun":
        return [("original_rerun", (), 0)]
    raise ValueError(phase)


def build_prompt(task, item, edits, seed):
    t = TASKS[task]
    instr, sep = build_instruction(t["sentences"], edits, seed, t["protected"])
    return instr + sep + item["input"]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model-tag", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18393)
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=100)
    ap.add_argument("--tasks", default="sst2,agnews,arc,squad")
    ap.add_argument("--phase", default="core")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="0,1")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=8)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    client = OpenAI(base_url=f"http://localhost:{args.port}/v1", api_key="local", timeout=900)
    seeds = [int(s) for s in args.seeds.split(",")]
    outdir = ROOT / "results" / "raw" / args.model_tag
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def call(prompt, max_tokens):
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                r = client.chat.completions.create(
                    model=args.model_tag, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
                    temperature=0.0, max_tokens=max_tokens, seed=42)
                return r.choices[0].message.content or "", r.usage.prompt_tokens, r.usage.completion_tokens
            except Exception as ex:  # transient server errors: back off and retry
                print(f"  retry {attempt}: {ex}", flush=True)
                time.sleep(5 * (attempt + 1))
        raise RuntimeError("server failed repeatedly")

    tasks = args.tasks.split(",")
    for cond, edits, seed in conditions(args.phase, seeds):
        for task in tasks:
            path = outdir / f"{task}.jsonl"
            done = set()
            if path.exists():
                done = {(d["condition"], d["item_id"]) for d in map(json.loads, open(path))}
            items = [it for it in load_items(task, args.n) if (cond, it["id"]) not in done]
            if not items:
                continue
            t0 = time.time()
            prompts = [build_prompt(task, it, edits, seed) for it in items]
            with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as ex, open(path, "a") as f:
                futs = {ex.submit(call, p, TASKS[task]["max_tokens"]): (it, p) for it, p in zip(items, prompts)}
                for fu in cf.as_completed(futs):
                    it, p = futs[fu]
                    out, pt, ct = fu.result()
                    sc = score(task, out, it["gold"])
                    rec = {"model": args.model_tag, "task": task, "task_type": TASKS[task]["type"],
                           "condition": cond, "edits": list(edits), "seed": seed, "item_id": it["id"],
                           "prompt": p, "output": out, "gold": it["gold"], "parsed": sc["parsed"],
                           "score": sc["score"], "em": sc["em"], "prompt_tokens": pt, "completion_tokens": ct}
                    f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
                    f.flush()
            print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {task:7s} {cond:18s} n={len(items)} "
                  f"{time.time() - t0:6.1f}s", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Planning: The Prompt Fragility Index (PFI)

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Practitioners routinely edit prompts (tidy whitespace, re-case, rephrase, reorder instructions) assuming
such edits are harmless. If some edit types silently change model accuracy by several points, then
(a) benchmark numbers reported with a single prompt are not reproducible, and (b) prompt maintenance in
production is risky. A per-edit-type, per-task-type fragility measure tells practitioners which edits
need re-validation and which are safe.

### Gap in Existing Work
(No literature review was pre-gathered for this run, the resource-finder stage was skipped and the
paper-search service returned no results, so this summary is from the author's knowledge of the field.)
Prior work shows LLMs are sensitive to prompt formatting (Sclar et al., 2024, "Quantifying Language
Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design" / FormatSpread), to paraphrased instructions
(Mizrahi et al., 2024, "State of What Art? A Call for Multi-Prompt LLM Evaluation"), to adversarial
character/word/sentence perturbations (Zhu et al., 2023, PromptBench), to few-shot ordering
(Lu et al., 2022), and proposes sensitivity scores (ProSA's PromptSensiScore, Zhuo et al., 2024; POSIX,
Chatterjee et al., 2024). Missing: a controlled, *benign*-edit taxonomy (the edits a human editor makes,
not adversarial attacks), compared on equal footing across task *types*, with an explicit test of
whether edit types **compound** super-additively when combined.

### Our Novel Contribution
1. A Prompt Fragility Index, PFI = relative performance drop of an edited prompt versus the original,
   reported per edit type × task type, along with an item-level flip rate.
2. A seeded edit generator in which a combined edit contains the same local edits as its single-edit
   counterparts, so the interaction (compounding) term can be measured directly:
   compounding ratio = drop(combo) / Σ drop(singles).

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (single edit types × 4 tasks): measures the main effect of each edit type. Needed for H1 (reorder/synonym > 8% vs. whitespace/caps < 1%).
- Exp 2 (task-type comparison): same edits on classification / multiple-choice / generation tasks. Needed for H2 (classification PFI ≈ 0.05 vs. generation PFI ≈ 0.22).
- Exp 3 (combinations of 2, 3 and 6 edit types): needed for H3 (3+ edits compound 30–50% beyond additive).
- Exp 4 (re-run of the original prompt): noise floor from server nondeterminism, so we don't attribute noise to edits.
- Exp 5 (if compute allows): a second model, to check generality.

## Research Question
How much do small, meaning-preserving edits to an instruction prompt (whitespace, capitalization,
punctuation, typos, synonym substitution, sentence reordering) change LLM task performance; does this

"""Analysis of prompt-fragility results.

Reads results/raw/<model>/*.jsonl and writes:
  results/summary_<model>.csv          per (task, condition) score, delta, PFI, flip rate
  results/edit_type_<model>.csv        per (task, edit type) pooled over seeds, bootstrap CI, tests
  results/task_type_<model>.csv        mean PFI per task type
  results/compounding_<model>.csv      combo delta vs sum of single-edit deltas
  figures/*.png
Usage: python src/analyze.py --model qwen2.5-1.5b
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from scipy import stats  # noqa: E402
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from perturb import EDIT_TYPES  # noqa: E402
from run_experiment import COMBOS  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RNG = np.random.default_rng(42)
B = 10000
TASK_ORDER = ["sst2", "agnews", "arc", "squad"]
TASK_TYPE = {"sst2": "classification", "agnews": "classification", "arc": "multiple_choice", "squad": "generation"}


def load(model):
    rows = []
    for f in sorted((ROOT / "results" / "raw" / model).glob("*.jsonl")):
        rows += [json.loads(l) for l in open(f)]
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df = df.drop_duplicates(["task", "condition", "item_id"], keep="first")
    return df


def wide(df, task):
    """item x condition matrix of scores for one task."""
    return df[df.task == task].pivot(index="item_id", columns="condition", values="score")


def boot_ci(x, stat=np.mean):
    x = np.asarray(x)
    idx = RNG.integers(0, len(x), size=(B, len(x)))
    bs = stat(x[idx], axis=1) if stat is np.mean else np.array([stat(x[i]) for i in idx])
    return np.percentile(bs, [2.5, 97.5])


def mcnemar_exact(a, b):
    """Exact McNemar test on paired binary vectors (a = original, b = edited)."""
    a, b = np.asarray(a).round().astype(int), np.asarray(b).round().astype(int)
    n01, n10 = int(((a == 1) & (b == 0)).sum()), int(((a == 0) & (b == 1)).sum())
    if n01 + n10 == 0:
        return 1.0
    return stats.binomtest(n01, n01 + n10, 0.5).pvalue


def paired_test(task, orig, edit):
    if task == "squad":
        d = np.asarray(orig) - np.asarray(edit)
        if np.allclose(d, 0):
            return 1.0
        return stats.wilcoxon(orig, edit, zero_method="zsplit").pvalue
    return mcnemar_exact(orig, edit)


def flip_rate(task, orig, edit):
    orig, edit = np.asarray(orig), np.asarray(edit)
    if task == "squad":  # a "flip" = F1 changes by >= 0.5 (correct <-> incorrect at the usual 0.5 threshold)
        return float(np.mean((orig >= 0.5) != (edit >= 0.5)))
    return float(np.mean(orig != edit))


def per_condition(df):
    out = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        W = wide(df, task)
        if "original" not in W:
            continue
        base = W["original"].mean()
        for cond in W.columns:
            col = W[cond].dropna()
            o = W.loc[col.index, "original"]
            d = (o - col).values
            out.append({"task": task, "task_type": TASK_TYPE[task], "condition": cond, "n": len(col),
                        "score": col.mean(), "orig_score": o.mean(), "delta_pts": 100 * d.mean(),
                        "pfi": d.mean() / base if base > 0 else np.nan,
                        "flip_rate": flip_rate(task, o.values, col.values),
                        "p_value": paired_test(task, o.values, col.values) if cond != "original" else np.nan})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def per_edit_type(df):
    """Pool the seeds of each single edit type: item-level delta averaged over seeds, then bootstrap over items."""
    out = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        W = wide(df, task)
        if "original" not in W:
            continue
        base = W["original"].mean()
        for e in EDIT_TYPES:
            cols = [c for c in W.columns if c.startswith(e + "@")]
            if not cols:
                continue
            sub = W[["original"] + cols].dropna()
            d = sub["original"].values[:, None] - sub[cols].values  # items x seeds
            dm = d.mean(axis=1)
            lo, hi = boot_ci(dm)
            ps = [paired_test(task, sub["original"].values, sub[c].values) for c in cols]
            # pooled test: stack (orig, edit) pairs across seeds
            pooled_p = paired_test(task, np.tile(sub["original"].values, len(cols)), sub[cols].values.T.ravel())
            out.append({"task": task, "task_type": TASK_TYPE[task], "edit": e, "n_items": len(sub),
                        "n_seeds": len(cols), "orig_score": base, "edited_score": sub[cols].values.mean(),
                        "delta_pts": 100 * dm.mean(), "ci_lo_pts": 100 * lo, "ci_hi_pts": 100 * hi,
                        "pfi": dm.mean() / base, "pfi_ci_lo": lo / base, "pfi_ci_hi": hi / base,
                        "abs_delta_pts_per_seed": 100 * np.abs(d.mean(axis=0)).mean(),
                        "flip_rate": np.mean([flip_rate(task, sub["original"].values, sub[c].values) for c in cols]),
                        "seed_deltas_pts": ";".join(f"{100 * x:.1f}" for x in d.mean(axis=0)),
                        "p_pooled": pooled_p, "p_min_seed": min(ps)})
    res = pd.DataFrame(out)
    if len(res):
        res["p_holm"] = multipletests(res["p_pooled"], method="holm")[1]
    return res


def compounding(df):
    """For each combo@seed: delta(combo) vs sum of delta(single@seed) for its components, per item -> bootstrap."""
    out = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        W = wide(df, task)
        if "original" not in W:
            continue
        for cname, comps in COMBOS.items():
            for c in [c for c in W.columns if c.startswith(cname + "@")]:
                s = c.split("@")[1]
                singles = [f"{e}@{s}" for e in comps]
                if not all(x in W for x in singles):
                    continue
                sub = W[["original", c] + singles].dropna()
                o = sub["original"].values
                d_combo = o - sub[c].values
                d_sum = sum(o - sub[x].values for x in singles)
                inter = d_combo - d_sum
                lo, hi = boot_ci(inter)
                max_single = max(o.mean() - sub[x].values.mean() for x in singles)
                out.append({"task": task, "task_type": TASK_TYPE[task], "combo": cname, "k": len(comps), "seed": int(s),
                            "delta_combo_pts": 100 * d_combo.mean(), "sum_single_pts": 100 * d_sum.mean(),
                            "max_single_pts": 100 * max_single,
                            "interaction_pts": 100 * inter.mean(), "inter_ci_lo": 100 * lo, "inter_ci_hi": 100 * hi,
                            "ratio": d_combo.mean() / d_sum.mean() if abs(d_sum.mean()) > 1e-9 else np.nan,
                            "flip_combo": flip_rate(task, o, sub[c].values),
                            "flip_sum_singles": sum(flip_rate(task, o, sub[x].values) for x in singles)})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def plots(model, cond, et, comp):
    fig_dir = ROOT / "figures"
    fig_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    tag = model.replace(".", "_")
    if len(et):
        # Heatmap of delta (points) edit type x task
        pv = et.pivot(index="edit", columns="task", values="delta_pts").reindex(index=EDIT_TYPES)
        pv = pv[[t for t in TASK_ORDER if t in pv]]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
        lim = max(1, np.nanmax(np.abs(pv.values)))
        im = ax.imshow(pv.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-lim, vmax=lim)
        ax.set_xticks(range(pv.shape[1]), [f"{t}\n({TASK_TYPE[t][:14]})" for t in pv.columns], fontsize=8)
        ax.set_yticks(range(pv.shape[0]), pv.index)
        for i in range(pv.shape[0]):
            for j in range(pv.shape[1]):
                ax.text(j, i, f"{pv.values[i, j]:+.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9)
        plt.colorbar(im, label="score drop vs. original (points; + = worse)")
        ax.set_title(f"Score drop by edit type ({model}, mean of 2 seeds)")
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"heatmap_delta_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

        # Bar chart with CIs
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(pv.columns), figsize=(3.2 * len(pv.columns), 3.6), sharey=False)
        for ax, task in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), pv.columns):
            sub = et[et.task == task].set_index("edit").reindex(EDIT_TYPES)
            y = sub["delta_pts"].values
            err = np.vstack([y - sub["ci_lo_pts"].values, sub["ci_hi_pts"].values - y])
            ax.bar(range(len(y)), y, yerr=err, color="#4C72B0", capsize=3)
            ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.8)
            ax.axhline(8, color="#C44E52", ls="--", lw=0.8)
            ax.axhline(1, color="#55A868", ls=":", lw=0.8)
            ax.set_xticks(range(len(y)), EDIT_TYPES, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=8)
            ax.set_title(f"{task} (orig={100 * sub['orig_score'].iloc[0]:.0f})", fontsize=10)
        np.atleast_1d(axes)[0].set_ylabel("drop (points), 95% bootstrap CI")
        fig.suptitle("Score drop per edit type; dashed red = 8-pt H1 threshold, dotted green = 1 pt", fontsize=9)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"bars_delta_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

        # Flip rate heatmap
        pf = et.pivot(index="edit", columns="task", values="flip_rate").reindex(index=EDIT_TYPES)[pv.columns]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
        im = ax.imshow(100 * pf.values, cmap="Oranges", vmin=0)
        ax.set_xticks(range(pf.shape[1]), pf.columns)
        ax.set_yticks(range(pf.shape[0]), pf.index)
        for i in range(pf.shape[0]):
            for j in range(pf.shape[1]):
                ax.text(j, i, f"{100 * pf.values[i, j]:.0f}%", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9)
        plt.colorbar(im, label="% items whose correctness flips")
        ax.set_title(f"Item-level flip rate ({model})")
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"heatmap_flip_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

    if len(comp):
        g = comp.groupby(["task", "combo", "k"], as_index=False)[["delta_combo_pts", "sum_single_pts"]].mean()
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 5))
        markers = {"sst2": "o", "agnews": "s", "arc": "^", "squad": "D"}
        for t, sub in g.groupby("task"):
            ax.scatter(sub["sum_single_pts"], sub["delta_combo_pts"], marker=markers[t], label=t, s=50)
            for _, r in sub.iterrows():
                ax.annotate(r["combo"], (r["sum_single_pts"], r["delta_combo_pts"]), fontsize=6, alpha=0.7)
        lo = min(g["sum_single_pts"].min(), g["delta_combo_pts"].min()) - 2
        hi = max(g["sum_single_pts"].max(), g["delta_combo_pts"].max()) + 2
        xs = np.linspace(lo, hi, 10)
        ax.plot(xs, xs, "k--", lw=1, label="additive (y=x)")
        ax.plot(xs, 1.4 * xs, color="#C44E52", ls=":", lw=1, label="H3: +40% (y=1.4x)")
        ax.set_xlabel("sum of single-edit drops (points)")
        ax.set_ylabel("combined-edit drop (points)")
        ax.set_title(f"Compounding of edits ({model})")
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"compounding_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    df = load(args.model)
    tag = args.model
    cond = per_condition(df)
    et = per_edit_type(df)
    comp = compounding(df)
    rdir = ROOT / "results"
    cond.to_csv(rdir / f"summary_{tag}.csv", index=False)
    et.to_csv(rdir / f"edit_type_{tag}.csv", index=False)
    comp.to_csv(rdir / f"compounding_{tag}.csv", index=False)
    if len(et):
        # Task-type PFI: mean over edit types of the pooled PFI; CI via bootstrap of items within task
        tt = et.groupby(["task", "task_type"], as_index=False).agg(
            mean_pfi=("pfi", "mean"), mean_abs_pfi=("pfi", lambda x: np.abs(x).mean()),
            mean_delta_pts=("delta_pts", "mean"), mean_flip=("flip_rate", "mean"), orig=("orig_score", "first"))
        tt.to_csv(rdir / f"task_type_{tag}.csv", index=False)
        print(tt.to_string(index=False))
    pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
    print(et[["task", "edit", "orig_score", "edited_score", "delta_pts", "ci_lo_pts", "ci_hi_pts", "pfi",
              "flip_rate", "seed_deltas_pts", "p_pooled", "p_holm"]].round(4).to_string(index=False))
    if len(comp):
        print(comp.round(3).to_string(index=False))
    plots(args.model, cond, et, comp)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Analysis of prompt-fragility results.

Reads results/raw/<model>/*.jsonl and writes:
  results/summary_<model>.csv          per (task, condition) score, delta, PFI, flip rate
  results/edit_type_<model>.csv        per (task, edit type) pooled over seeds, bootstrap CI, tests
  results/task_type_<model>.csv        mean PFI per task type
  results/compounding_<model>.csv      combo delta vs sum of single-edit deltas
  figures/*.png
Usage: python src/analyze.py --model qwen2.5-1.5b
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from scipy import stats  # noqa: E402
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from perturb import EDIT_TYPES  # noqa: E402
from run_experiment import COMBOS  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RNG = np.random.default_rng(42)
B = 10000
TASK_ORDER = ["sst2", "agnews", "arc", "squad"]
TASK_TYPE = {"sst2": "classification", "agnews": "classification", "arc": "multiple_choice", "squad": "generation"}


def load(model):
    rows = []
    for f in sorted((ROOT / "results" / "raw" / model).glob("*.jsonl")):
        rows += [json.loads(l) for l in open(f)]
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df = df.drop_duplicates(["task", "condition", "item_id"], keep="first")
    return df


def wide(df, task):
    """item x condition matrix of scores for one task."""
    return df[df.task == task].pivot(index="item_id", columns="condition", values="score")


def boot_ci(x, stat=np.mean):
    x = np.asarray(x)
    idx = RNG.integers(0, len(x), size=(B, len(x)))
    bs = stat(x[idx], axis=1) if stat is np.mean else np.array([stat(x[i]) for i in idx])
    return np.percentile(bs, [2.5, 97.5])


def mcnemar_exact(a, b):
    """Exact McNemar test on paired binary vectors (a = original, b = edited)."""
    a, b = np.asarray(a).round().astype(int), np.asarray(b).round().astype(int)
    n01, n10 = int(((a == 1) & (b == 0)).sum()), int(((a == 0) & (b == 1)).sum())
    if n01 + n10 == 0:
        return 1.0
    return stats.binomtest(n01, n01 + n10, 0.5).pvalue


def paired_test(task, orig, edit):
    if task == "squad":
        d = np.asarray(orig) - np.asarray(edit)
        if np.allclose(d, 0):
            return 1.0
        return stats.wilcoxon(orig, edit, zero_method="zsplit").pvalue
    return mcnemar_exact(orig, edit)


def flip_rate(task, orig, edit):
    orig, edit = np.asarray(orig), np.asarray(edit)
    if task == "squad":  # a "flip" = F1 changes by >= 0.5 (correct <-> incorrect at the usual 0.5 threshold)
        return float(np.mean((orig >= 0.5) != (edit >= 0.5)))
    return float(np.mean(orig != edit))


def per_condition(df):
    out = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        W = wide(df, task)
        if "original" not in W:
            continue
        base = W["original"].mean()
        for cond in W.columns:
            col = W[cond].dropna()
            o = W.loc[col.index, "original"]
            d = (o - col).values
            out.append({"task": task, "task_type": TASK_TYPE[task], "condition": cond, "n": len(col),
                        "score": col.mean(), "orig_score": o.mean(), "delta_pts": 100 * d.mean(),
                        "pfi": d.mean() / base if base > 0 else np.nan,
                        "flip_rate": flip_rate(task, o.values, col.values),
                        "p_value": paired_test(task, o.values, col.values) if cond != "original" else np.nan})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def per_edit_type(df):
    """Pool the seeds of each single edit type: item-level delta averaged over seeds, then bootstrap over items."""
    out = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        W = wide(df, task)
        if "original" not in W:
            continue
        base = W["original"].mean()
        for e in EDIT_TYPES:
            cols = [c for c in W.columns if c.startswith(e + "@")]
            if not cols:
                continue
            sub = W[["original"] + cols].dropna()
            d = sub["original"].values[:, None] - sub[cols].values  # items x seeds
            dm = d.mean(axis=1)
            lo, hi = boot_ci(dm)
            ps = [paired_test(task, sub["original"].values, sub[c].values) for c in cols]
            # pooled test: stack (orig, edit) pairs across seeds
            pooled_p = paired_test(task, np.tile(sub["original"].values, len(cols)), sub[cols].values.T.ravel())
            out.append({"task": task, "task_type": TASK_TYPE[task], "edit": e, "n_items": len(sub),
                        "n_seeds": len(cols), "orig_score": base, "edited_score": sub[cols].values.mean(),
                        "delta_pts": 100 * dm.mean(), "ci_lo_pts": 100 * lo, "ci_hi_pts": 100 * hi,
                        "pfi": dm.mean() / base, "pfi_ci_lo": lo / base, "pfi_ci_hi": hi / base,
                        "abs_delta_pts_per_seed": 100 * np.abs(d.mean(axis=0)).mean(),
                        "flip_rate": np.mean([flip_rate(task, sub["original"].values, sub[c].values) for c in cols]),
                        "seed_deltas_pts": ";".join(f"{100 * x:.1f}" for x in d.mean(axis=0)),
                        "p_pooled": pooled_p, "p_min_seed": min(ps)})
    res = pd.DataFrame(out)
    if len(res):
        res["p_holm"] = multipletests(res["p_pooled"], method="holm")[1]
    return res

    out = []

                            "max_single_pts": 100 * max_single,
                            "interaction_pts": 100 * inter.mean(), "inter_ci_lo": 100 * lo, "inter_ci_hi": 100 * hi,
                            "ratio": d_combo.mean() / d_sum.mean() if abs(d_sum.mean()) > 1e-9 else np.nan,
                            "flip_combo": flip_rate(task, o, sub[c].values),
                            "flip_sum_singles": sum(flip_rate(task, o, sub[x].values) for x in singles)})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

        plt.colorbar(im, label="score drop vs. original (points; + = worse)")
        ax.set_title(f"Score drop by edit type ({model}, mean of 2 seeds)")

        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"heatmap_delta_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"bars_delta_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

        # Flip rate heatmap
        pf = et.pivot(index="edit", columns="task", values="flip_rate").reindex(index=EDIT_TYPES)[pv.columns]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
        im = ax.imshow(100 * pf.values, cmap="Oranges", vmin=0)

        for i in range(pf.shape[0]):

        plt.colorbar(im, label="% items whose correctness flips")
        ax.set_title(f"Item-level flip rate ({model})")
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"heatmap_flip_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

    if len(comp):
        g = comp.groupby(["task", "combo", "k"], as_index=False)[["delta_combo_pts", "sum_single_pts"]].mean()
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 5))

#!/bin/bash
# chain.sh <wait_pid> <model_tag> <port> <job> [<job> ...]
# Waits for a running runner to exit, then runs jobs sequentially on one server.
# A job is "task:phase:seeds", e.g. "sst2:combos:0,1".
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
source .venv/bin/activate
WAIT=$1; MODEL=$2; PORT=$3; shift 3
while kill -0 "$WAIT" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 15; done
for JOB in "$@"; do
  IFS=: read -r T PH S <<< "$JOB"
  python src/run_experiment.py --model-tag "$MODEL" --port "$PORT" --n 100 --tasks "$T" --phase "$PH" --seeds "$S" --workers 6 \
    >> "logs/run_${MODEL}_${PH}_${T}.log" 2>&1
done

"""Error analysis: parse failures, label-distribution shifts, edit magnitude vs. effect, flip examples.

Usage: python src/error_analysis.py --model qwen2.5-1.5b
Writes results/error_analysis_<model>.md and results/edit_magnitude_<model>.csv
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from analyze import load, TASK_ORDER  # noqa: E402
from perturb import build_instruction, char_edit_distance_ratio  # noqa: E402
from run_experiment import COMBOS  # noqa: E402
from tasks import TASKS  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def edits_of(cond):
    name, seed = cond.split("@") if "@" in cond else (cond, "0")
    if name in COMBOS:
        return COMBOS[name], int(seed)
    if name.startswith("original"):
        return (), 0
    return (name,), int(seed)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    df = load(args.model)
    lines = [f"# Error analysis: {args.model}\n"]

    # 1. Parse failures (no recognizable label/letter) per task x condition
    lines.append("## Parse-failure rate (% of outputs with no recognizable label/letter)\n")
    cls = df[df.task != "squad"].copy()
    cls["fail"] = cls["parsed"].isna()
    pf = cls.pivot_table(index="condition", columns="task", values="fail", aggfunc="mean") * 100
    lines.append(pf.round(1).to_markdown() + "\n")

    # 2. Prediction distribution shifts (classification)
    lines.append("## Predicted-label distribution per condition\n")
    for task in ["sst2", "agnews", "arc"]:
        sub = df[df.task == task]
        if sub.empty:
            continue
        tab = sub.assign(parsed=sub["parsed"].fillna("NONE")).pivot_table(
            index="condition", columns="parsed", values="item_id", aggfunc="count", fill_value=0)
        lines.append(f"### {task}\n\n" + tab.to_markdown() + "\n")

    # 3. SQuAD output length (verbosity) per condition
    sq = df[df.task == "squad"]
    if len(sq):
        lines.append("## SQuAD: mean output length (words) and EM per condition\n")
        t = sq.assign(len_words=sq["output"].str.split().str.len()).groupby("condition").agg(
            f1=("score", "mean"), em=("em", "mean"), len_words=("len_words", "mean"))
        lines.append(t.round(3).to_markdown() + "\n")

    # 4. Edit magnitude vs. effect
    mag = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        sub = df[df.task == task]
        if sub.empty or "original" not in set(sub.condition):
            continue
        orig_instr, _ = build_instruction(TASKS[task]["sentences"], (), 0, TASKS[task]["protected"])
        base = sub[sub.condition == "original"].set_index("item_id")["score"]
        for cond in sorted(set(sub.condition) - {"original", "original_rerun"}):
            ed, seed = edits_of(cond)
            instr, _ = build_instruction(TASKS[task]["sentences"], ed, seed, TASKS[task]["protected"])
            s = sub[sub.condition == cond].set_index("item_id")["score"]
            common = base.index.intersection(s.index)
            mag.append({"task": task, "condition": cond, "k_edits": len(ed),
                        "char_dist": char_edit_distance_ratio(orig_instr, instr),
                        "delta_pts": 100 * (base[common] - s[common]).mean(),
                        "flip": float(((base[common] >= 0.5) != (s[common] >= 0.5)).mean())})
    mag = pd.DataFrame(mag)
    mag.to_csv(ROOT / "results" / f"edit_magnitude_{args.model}.csv", index=False)
    if len(mag) > 3:
        r1 = stats.spearmanr(mag.char_dist, mag.delta_pts)
        r2 = stats.spearmanr(mag.char_dist, mag.flip)
        lines.append("## Edit magnitude vs. effect (all perturbed conditions, all tasks)\n")
        lines.append(f"Spearman(char edit distance, drop) = {r1.statistic:.3f} (p={r1.pvalue:.3g}); "
                     f"Spearman(char edit distance, flip rate) = {r2.statistic:.3f} (p={r2.pvalue:.3g}); n={len(mag)}\n")

    # 5. Example flips (correct under original -> wrong under edit) for the most damaging condition per task
    lines.append("## Example flips (original correct -> edited wrong)\n")
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        m = mag[mag.task == task] if len(mag) else mag
        if m.empty:
            continue
        worst = m.sort_values("delta_pts").iloc[-1]["condition"]
        sub = df[df.task == task]
        o = sub[sub.condition == "original"].set_index("item_id")
        e = sub[sub.condition == worst].set_index("item_id")
        common = o.index.intersection(e.index)
        flips = [i for i in common if o.loc[i, "score"] >= 0.5 > e.loc[i, "score"]][:3]
        lines.append(f"### {task}: worst condition = `{worst}`\n")
        lines.append("Edited prompt instruction (first item):\n\n```\n" +
                     e.loc[common[0], "prompt"].split("Review:")[0].split("Article:")[0].split("Question:")[0]
                     .split("Passage:")[0][:600] + "\n```\n")
        for i in flips:
            gold = o.loc[i, "gold"] if task != "squad" else o.loc[i, "gold"][0]
            lines.append(f"- `{i}` gold=`{gold}` | original→`{o.loc[i, 'output'][:60]!s}` | edited→`{e.loc[i, 'output'][:60]!s}`")
        lines.append("")

    out = ROOT / "results" / f"error_analysis_{args.model}.md"
    out.write_text("\n".join(lines))
    print("\n".join(lines)[:6000])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

name: neurico-host-local-llm-fallback
description: On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent and CPU is saturated; how local llama.cpp fallback performed and process-kill pitfall
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Observed 2026-10-14 in a neurico research workspace on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env, and `~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` had `# OPENROUTER_KEY=[REDACTED] commented out. Fallback that worked: llama.cpp release binary (ggml-org b11624 ubuntu-x64) downloaded into the workspace `tools/`, GGUF models cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (bartowski Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B Q8_0).
- No GPU; 32 cores shared by many sessions (load avg ~60). Per-process throughput was tiny (~40 prefill tok/s); more threads per server did not help, but several independent servers (6–8 threads each) scaled aggregate throughput. `transformers` CPU generation was much slower than llama.cpp.
- Pitfall: `pkill -f <pattern>` (or `ps|grep|xargs kill`) inside a Bash call whose own command text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (exit 144). Find PIDs in one call, kill by PID in a separate call.

"""Analysis of prompt-fragility results.

Reads results/raw/<model>/*.jsonl and writes:
  results/summary_<model>.csv          per (task, condition) score, delta, PFI, flip rate
  results/edit_type_<model>.csv        per (task, edit type) pooled over seeds, bootstrap CI, tests
  results/task_type_<model>.csv        mean PFI per task type
  results/compounding_<model>.csv      combo delta vs sum of single-edit deltas
  figures/*.png
Usage: python src/analyze.py --model qwen2.5-1.5b
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from scipy import stats  # noqa: E402
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from perturb import EDIT_TYPES  # noqa: E402
from run_experiment import COMBOS  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RNG = np.random.default_rng(42)
B = 10000
TASK_ORDER = ["sst2", "agnews", "arc", "squad"]
TASK_TYPE = {"sst2": "classification", "agnews": "classification", "arc": "multiple_choice", "squad": "generation"}


def load(model):
    rows = []
    for f in sorted((ROOT / "results" / "raw" / model).glob("*.jsonl")):
        rows += [json.loads(l) for l in open(f)]
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df = df.drop_duplicates(["task", "condition", "item_id"], keep="first")
    return df


def wide(df, task):
    """item x condition matrix of scores for one task."""
    return df[df.task == task].pivot(index="item_id", columns="condition", values="score")


def boot_ci(x, stat=np.mean):
    x = np.asarray(x)
    idx = RNG.integers(0, len(x), size=(B, len(x)))
    bs = stat(x[idx], axis=1) if stat is np.mean else np.array([stat(x[i]) for i in idx])
    return np.percentile(bs, [2.5, 97.5])


def mcnemar_exact(a, b):
    """Exact McNemar test on paired binary vectors (a = original, b = edited)."""
    a, b = np.asarray(a).round().astype(int), np.asarray(b).round().astype(int)
    n01, n10 = int(((a == 1) & (b == 0)).sum()), int(((a == 0) & (b == 1)).sum())
    if n01 + n10 == 0:
        return 1.0
    return stats.binomtest(n01, n01 + n10, 0.5).pvalue


def paired_test(task, orig, edit):
    if task == "squad":
        d = np.asarray(orig) - np.asarray(edit)
        if np.allclose(d, 0):
            return 1.0
        return stats.wilcoxon(orig, edit, zero_method="zsplit").pvalue
    return mcnemar_exact(orig, edit)


def flip_rate(task, orig, edit):
    orig, edit = np.asarray(orig), np.asarray(edit)
    if task == "squad":  # a "flip" = F1 changes by >= 0.5 (correct <-> incorrect at the usual 0.5 threshold)
        return float(np.mean((orig >= 0.5) != (edit >= 0.5)))
    return float(np.mean(orig != edit))


def per_condition(df):
    out = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        W = wide(df, task)
        if "original" not in W:
            continue
        base = W["original"].mean()
        for cond in W.columns:
            col = W[cond].dropna()
            o = W.loc[col.index, "original"]
            d = (o - col).values
            out.append({"task": task, "task_type": TASK_TYPE[task], "condition": cond, "n": len(col),
                        "score": col.mean(), "orig_score": o.mean(), "delta_pts": 100 * d.mean(),
                        "pfi": d.mean() / base if base > 0 else np.nan,
                        "flip_rate": flip_rate(task, o.values, col.values),
                        "p_value": paired_test(task, o.values, col.values) if cond != "original" else np.nan})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def per_edit_type(df):
    """Pool the seeds of each single edit type: item-level delta averaged over seeds, then bootstrap over items."""
    out = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        W = wide(df, task)
        if "original" not in W:
            continue
        base = W["original"].mean()
        for e in EDIT_TYPES:
            cols = [c for c in W.columns if c.startswith(e + "@")]
            if not cols:
                continue
            sub = W[["original"] + cols].dropna()
            d = sub["original"].values[:, None] - sub[cols].values  # items x seeds
            dm = d.mean(axis=1)
            lo, hi = boot_ci(dm)
            ps = [paired_test(task, sub["original"].values, sub[c].values) for c in cols]
            # pooled test: stack (orig, edit) pairs across seeds
            pooled_p = paired_test(task, np.tile(sub["original"].values, len(cols)), sub[cols].values.T.ravel())
            out.append({"task": task, "task_type": TASK_TYPE[task], "edit": e, "n_items": len(sub),
                        "n_seeds": len(cols), "orig_score": base, "edited_score": sub[cols].values.mean(),
                        "delta_pts": 100 * dm.mean(), "ci_lo_pts": 100 * lo, "ci_hi_pts": 100 * hi,
                        "pfi": dm.mean() / base, "pfi_ci_lo": lo / base, "pfi_ci_hi": hi / base,
                        "abs_delta_pts_per_seed": 100 * np.abs(d.mean(axis=0)).mean(),
                        "flip_rate": np.mean([flip_rate(task, sub["original"].values, sub[c].values) for c in cols]),
                        "seed_deltas_pts": ";".join(f"{100 * x:.1f}" for x in d.mean(axis=0)),
                        "p_pooled": pooled_p, "p_min_seed": min(ps)})
    res = pd.DataFrame(out)
    if len(res):
        res["p_holm"] = multipletests(res["p_pooled"], method="holm")[1]
    return res


def compounding(df):
    """For each combo@seed: delta(combo) vs sum of delta(single@seed) for its components, per item -> bootstrap."""
    out = []
    for task in TASK_ORDER:
        W = wide(df, task)
        if "original" not in W:
            continue
        for cname, comps in COMBOS.items():
            for c in [c for c in W.columns if c.startswith(cname + "@")]:
                s = c.split("@")[1]
                singles = [f"{e}@{s}" for e in comps]
                if not all(x in W for x in singles):
                    continue
                sub = W[["original", c] + singles].dropna()
                o = sub["original"].values
                d_combo = o - sub[c].values
                d_sum = sum(o - sub[x].values for x in singles)
                inter = d_combo - d_sum
                lo, hi = boot_ci(inter)
                max_single = max(o.mean() - sub[x].values.mean() for x in singles)
                out.append({"task": task, "task_type": TASK_TYPE[task], "combo": cname, "k": len(comps), "seed": int(s),
                            "delta_combo_pts": 100 * d_combo.mean(), "sum_single_pts": 100 * d_sum.mean(),
                            "max_single_pts": 100 * max_single,
                            "interaction_pts": 100 * inter.mean(), "inter_ci_lo": 100 * lo, "inter_ci_hi": 100 * hi,
                            "ratio": d_combo.mean() / d_sum.mean() if abs(d_sum.mean()) > 1e-9 else np.nan,
                            "flip_combo": flip_rate(task, o, sub[c].values),
                            "flip_sum_singles": sum(flip_rate(task, o, sub[x].values) for x in singles)})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def plots(model, cond, et, comp):
    fig_dir = ROOT / "figures"
    fig_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    tag = model.replace(".", "_")
    if len(et):
        # Heatmap of delta (points) edit type x task
        pv = et.pivot(index="edit", columns="task", values="delta_pts").reindex(index=EDIT_TYPES)
        pv = pv[[t for t in TASK_ORDER if t in pv]]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
        lim = max(1, np.nanmax(np.abs(pv.values)))
        im = ax.imshow(pv.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-lim, vmax=lim)
        ax.set_xticks(range(pv.shape[1]), [f"{t}\n({TASK_TYPE[t][:14]})" for t in pv.columns], fontsize=8)
        ax.set_yticks(range(pv.shape[0]), pv.index)
        for i in range(pv.shape[0]):
            for j in range(pv.shape[1]):
                ax.text(j, i, f"{pv.values[i, j]:+.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9)
        plt.colorbar(im, label="score drop vs. original (points; + = worse)")
        ax.set_title(f"Score drop by edit type ({model}, mean of 2 seeds)")
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"heatmap_delta_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

        # Bar chart with CIs
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(pv.columns), figsize=(3.2 * len(pv.columns), 3.6), sharey=False)
        for ax, task in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), pv.columns):
            sub = et[et.task == task].set_index("edit").reindex(EDIT_TYPES)
            y = sub["delta_pts"].values
            err = np.vstack([y - sub["ci_lo_pts"].values, sub["ci_hi_pts"].values - y])
            ax.bar(range(len(y)), y, yerr=err, color="#4C72B0", capsize=3)
            ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.8)
            ax.axhline(8, color="#C44E52", ls="--", lw=0.8)
            ax.axhline(1, color="#55A868", ls=":", lw=0.8)
            ax.set_xticks(range(len(y)), EDIT_TYPES, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=8)
            ax.set_title(f"{task} (orig={100 * sub['orig_score'].iloc[0]:.0f})", fontsize=10)
        np.atleast_1d(axes)[0].set_ylabel("drop (points), 95% bootstrap CI")
        fig.suptitle("Score drop per edit type; dashed red = 8-pt H1 threshold, dotted green = 1 pt", fontsize=9)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"bars_delta_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

        # Flip rate heatmap
        pf = et.pivot(index="edit", columns="task", values="flip_rate").reindex(index=EDIT_TYPES)[pv.columns]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
        im = ax.imshow(100 * pf.values, cmap="Oranges", vmin=0)
        ax.set_xticks(range(pf.shape[1]), pf.columns)
        ax.set_yticks(range(pf.shape[0]), pf.index)
        for i in range(pf.shape[0]):
            for j in range(pf.shape[1]):
                ax.text(j, i, f"{100 * pf.values[i, j]:.0f}%", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9)
        plt.colorbar(im, label="% items whose correctness flips")
        ax.set_title(f"Item-level flip rate ({model})")
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"heatmap_flip_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()

    if len(comp):
        g = comp.groupby(["task", "combo", "k"], as_index=False)[["delta_combo_pts", "sum_single_pts"]].mean()
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 5))
        markers = {"sst2": "o", "agnews": "s", "arc": "^", "squad": "D"}
        for t, sub in g.groupby("task"):
            ax.scatter(sub["sum_single_pts"], sub["delta_combo_pts"], marker=markers[t], label=t, s=50)
            for _, r in sub.iterrows():
                ax.annotate(r["combo"], (r["sum_single_pts"], r["delta_combo_pts"]), fontsize=6, alpha=0.7)
        lo = min(g["sum_single_pts"].min(), g["delta_combo_pts"].min()) - 2
        hi = max(g["sum_single_pts"].max(), g["delta_combo_pts"].max()) + 2
        xs = np.linspace(lo, hi, 10)
        ax.plot(xs, xs, "k--", lw=1, label="additive (y=x)")
        ax.plot(xs, 1.4 * xs, color="#C44E52", ls=":", lw=1, label="H3: +40% (y=1.4x)")
        ax.set_xlabel("sum of single-edit drops (points)")
        ax.set_ylabel("combined-edit drop (points)")
        ax.set_title(f"Compounding of edits ({model})")
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fig_dir / f"compounding_{tag}.png", dpi=150)
        plt.close()


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    df = load(args.model)
    tag = args.model
    cond = per_condition(df)
    et = per_edit_type(df)
    comp = compounding(df)
    rdir = ROOT / "results"
    cond.to_csv(rdir / f"summary_{tag}.csv", index=False)
    et.to_csv(rdir / f"edit_type_{tag}.csv", index=False)
    comp.to_csv(rdir / f"compounding_{tag}.csv", index=False)
    if len(et):
        # Task-type PFI: mean over edit types of the pooled PFI; CI via bootstrap of items within task
        tt = et.groupby(["task", "task_type"], as_index=False).agg(
            mean_pfi=("pfi", "mean"), mean_abs_pfi=("pfi", lambda x: np.abs(x).mean()),
            mean_delta_pts=("delta_pts", "mean"), mean_flip=("flip_rate", "mean"), orig=("orig_score", "first"))
        tt.to_csv(rdir / f"task_type_{tag}.csv", index=False)
        print(tt.to_string(index=False))
    pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
    print(et[["task", "edit", "orig_score", "edited_score", "delta_pts", "ci_lo_pts", "ci_hi_pts", "pfi",
              "flip_rate", "seed_deltas_pts", "p_pooled", "p_holm"]].round(4).to_string(index=False))
    if len(comp):
        print(comp.round(3).to_string(index=False))
    plots(args.model, cond, et, comp)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Reads results/raw/<model>/*.jsonl and writes:
  results/summary_<model>.csv          per (task, condition) score, delta, PFI, flip rate
  results/edit_type_<model>.csv        per (task, edit type) pooled over seeds, bootstrap CI, tests
  results/task_type_<model>.csv        mean PFI per task type

Usage: python src/analyze.py --model qwen2.5-1.5b
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from scipy import stats  # noqa: E402
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests  # noqa: E402
